newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analyst sees Krupp bid for Thyssen as share swap.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees Krupp bid for Thyssen as share swap.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp would be unlikely to make a cash offer for rival Thyssen AG in any takeover bid, a German equities analyst said on Monday.

Volker Firchau, analyst with regional bank Bayerische Landesbank, told Germany's N-TV news channel that although Krupp has significantly reduced its debt since the 1991 takeover of Hoesch, it would not likely pay cash for Thyssen.

"Krupp-Hoesch has been very successful in restructuring but it still has problems in its ratio of capital to equity," Firchau said. "That's why I think it would be more likely to be a share swap than a cash payment."
Earlier, Thyssen said it had information that Krupp was about to make a hostile takeover bid and called a news conference for Tuesday at 1400 GMT.

Firchau said a merger of Germany's two largest steel makers could pave the way for cost reduction needed to improve Germany's competitiveness compared to other European steel makers, particularly British steel.
"In the steel industry, Germany is operating with a cost structure that is not competitive," he said. (( -- William Boston, Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097 145 ))
